newsitem.title: UK: Russian debt sets new highs as closing draws nearer.
newsitem.headline: Russian debt sets new highs as closing draws nearer.

text.p: Russian loans surged late on Wednesday on news it had fully reconciled about 60 percent of its debt with the London Club bringing a final debt restructing agreement one step closer, experts said.
"Evidently, the market is interpreting this as a pretty positive sign," said David Boren, vice president of economic and market analysis at Salomon Brothers Inc.
Indeed, Russian Vneshekonombank dollar-denominated debt surged 3/4 to record highs of 95-1/8 bid and the country's PRINs jumped 3/4 to a record level of 70-1/4 bid.

"The market is rallying and I think the perception is not simply that Vneshekonombank has agreed to 60 percent but that 60 percent has been agreed to by Vneshekonombank and that the creditors had responded," Boren added.
In a news report from Moscow, Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov told Reuters the figure reconciled was nearing 60 percent and the exact figure would be announced in the middle of next week.

In order for the debt restructuring to be finalized, Russia has to fully reconcile 90 percent of the $24 billion principal of its total $35 billion of debt owed to the London Club of commercial bank creditors.

Emerging market analysts said the fact that the Russian Finance Ministry has promised to start publishing fully reconciled debt volumes every week beginning in August was also viewed positively by the market.

"If they are going to give the market every week an indication of how they are progressing that is very positive because that introduces a much greater deal of transparency," said Ingrid Iverson, emerging Europe debt strategist, at UBS Securities in London.
